No, not as a current conclusion. Your June 2025 finding was accurate for what it covered: no loss of 0.5 ha or more was detected from 2021 to 2024. It has since been superseded.

The updated evidence (as of 2026-11-12) extends the period through 2025 and shows a tree-cover loss candidate of 13.5 ha in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha property. The JRC 2020 forest reference agrees with the location at 0.98.

Caveats:
- The loss is pending corroboration. It falls in the latest year of the series, so a later year is needed to confirm it is persistent.
- It does not show deforestation or land-use change. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation.
- It does not show the cause or whether the change was legal.
- It is not a compliance finding.

I'd update the file to say the 2021–2024 result stands, but a 2025 loss candidate is open and needs follow-up.
